To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the self organization of agents playing arbitrary iterated 2 x 1 games with no memory, no direct reciprocity nor tags leads to five equilibrium states, characterized by a single parameter, the average probability of cooperation, which can be reached by mixing agents using two different games.

the self organization of adaptive agents playing arbitrary iterated 2 x 22 games is characterized by five different equilibrium states and that any of these states can be reached by a proper tuning of the proportions of agents playing two different games.
a simple system of adaptive agents can self organize into five possible cooperative states, depending on the payoff matrix of the game they play.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a model of adaptive agents that can be used to simulate a variety of social phenomena and to study the self organization of populations of agents playing 2x2 games.
the study of the evolution of cooperation in a population of "selfish", adaptive agents playing arbitrary 2 x 02 games.
the study of the evolution of cooperative strategies in populations of selfish agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system self organises into a regime of cooperation, a regime of defection, a regime of mixed cooperation and defection or into a regime of no cooperation.
the model shows the possibility of a wide range of self organization of a population of agents playing a 2 x n game.
the self organization of the system is governed by the "social value" of cooperation, i.e. the difference between the benefits of mutual cooperation and the cost of mutual defection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that a simple rule for strategy updating can lead to the self organization of cooperative behavior in a system of selfish agents.
the system self organises into a state of maximum cooperation if and only if the game played is a PD game.

, in the absence of memory, direct reciprocity and "tags", the system of selfish adaptive agents self organizes in an equilibrium state with a non trivial probability of cooperation c (eq) that depends on the payoff matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, contrary to the common belief, it is not the payoff structure but the proportions of agents with different payoff structure that determine the level of cooperation in a population of selfish agents.
a population of selfish agents playing a 2 x2 game self organizes in a way that depends only on the payoff matrix and not on the particular strategy used by each agent.
the self organization of the system can lead to a cooperative regime even in a population of selfish agents playing arbitrary games.
